topic: 6 strange borders countdown ending at Longwa, Nagaland
hook: Your night in Longwa village, Nagaland, can put your head in India and your feet in Myanmar.
title: 6 Borders That Make No Sense (Last One Is in India)
description:
A countdown of six real borders that look fake on a map: a runway you walk across, a Russian region cut off from Russia, a Spanish town inside France, a German village inside Switzerland, an enclave inside an enclave, and a chief's house in Nagaland where the India-Myanmar line runs through the building. Every place in this video is real and you can find it on a map. Watch to the end for India's strangest border.

#borders #geography #strangeplaces
comment_prompt: Which border was the strangest: 1 to 6?

scenes.narration: Your night in Longwa village, Nagaland, can put your head in India and your feet in Myanmar.
scenes.headline: ONE BED, TWO COUNTRIES

scenes.narration: That is not a joke. A real border line runs straight through a real house, and real people live there.
scenes.headline: A BORDER THROUGH A HOUSE

scenes.narration: Today I will count down six borders that make no sense, from a runway you walk across to a village inside another country.
scenes.headline: 6 BORDERS, COUNTDOWN

scenes.narration: Each one is stranger than the one before it, and you can find every one of them on a normal map.
scenes.headline: ALL OF THEM ARE REAL

scenes.narration: The last one is in India. By the end, you will see why a chief's house beats all the others.
scenes.headline: NUMBER ONE IS INDIA

scenes.narration: Let us start at number six, and the strange part is that you can walk right across it.
scenes.headline: LET'S START

scenes.narration: Number six. Gibraltar. To walk from Spain into Gibraltar, you cross an active airport runway on foot.
scenes.headline: GIBRALTAR

scenes.narration: Yes, a runway. The main road into Gibraltar cuts straight across the strip where planes land and take off.
scenes.headline: ROAD ACROSS A RUNWAY

scenes.narration: Gibraltar belongs to the United Kingdom, but it sits at the southern tip of Spain, joined to the Spanish mainland.
scenes.headline: UK LAND IN SPAIN

scenes.narration: So the border is a narrow neck of land, and the airport was built right across it.
scenes.headline: A NARROW NECK OF LAND

scenes.narration: When a plane is about to land or take off, barriers come down and the road closes. Cars, bikes and people just wait.
scenes.headline: BARRIERS COME DOWN

scenes.narration: Then the plane is gone, the barriers lift, and everyone goes back to crossing a country border like nothing happened.
scenes.headline: THEN LIFE GOES ON

scenes.narration: Picture it: you are in the queue for passport check, and a jet rushes past right in front of you.
scenes.headline: PASSPORT QUEUE + JET

scenes.narration: The reason is size. Gibraltar is tiny, so a road and a runway had to share the same flat ground.
scenes.headline: TOO SMALL TO SEPARATE

scenes.narration: It is a rare place where an airport, a road and a country border all fit into one spot.
scenes.headline: THREE THINGS, ONE SPOT

scenes.narration: Now think about how odd that is. A plane lands where people were walking from one country to another a minute ago.
scenes.headline: WALKING WHERE JETS LAND

scenes.narration: But a runway is at least on land that connects to its own country. The next place does not even have that.
scenes.headline: IT GETS WORSE

scenes.narration: Number five is a piece of Russia with no land link to Russia.
scenes.headline: NEXT: A CUT-OFF RUSSIA

scenes.narration: Number five. Kaliningrad, a piece of Russia that is not connected to the rest of Russia by land.
scenes.headline: KALININGRAD

scenes.narration: It sits on the Baltic coast, with Poland on one side and Lithuania on the other.
scenes.headline: POLAND AND LITHUANIA

scenes.narration: Both are in the European Union and NATO, so this Russian region is surrounded by them, except for the sea.
scenes.headline: SURROUNDED, EXCEPT SEA

scenes.narration: The reason goes back to the end of the Second World War, when this area was taken from Germany.
scenes.headline: WORLD WAR TWO LEFTOVER

scenes.narration: Then the Soviet Union broke up in 1991, and the lands between Kaliningrad and Russia became independent countries.
scenes.headline: THE USSR BREAKS UP

scenes.narration: Overnight, a region that was once joined by Soviet land was suddenly cut off by new borders.
scenes.headline: CUT OFF OVERNIGHT

scenes.narration: Today, a train or truck going between Kaliningrad and the rest of Russia has to cross other countries, or go by sea or air.
scenes.headline: NO DIRECT ROAD HOME

scenes.narration: The city's old name was Königsberg, and it was a German city for centuries before that.
scenes.headline: ONCE KÖNIGSBERG

scenes.narration: So an old German city now sits in Russia, on the far side of Poland and Lithuania from Moscow.
scenes.headline: A GERMAN CITY IN RUSSIA

scenes.narration: Imagine a piece of India that you could only reach by crossing two other countries first.
scenes.headline: IMAGINE THIS FOR INDIA

scenes.narration: That is the kind of map problem that politicians still argue about today.
scenes.headline: STILL ARGUED ABOUT

scenes.narration: But that is a whole region. Next, a single Spanish town that is surrounded by France.
scenes.headline: A TOWN INSIDE FRANCE

scenes.narration: Number four. Llívia, a Spanish town that sits completely inside France.
scenes.headline: LLÍVIA

scenes.narration: Walk to the edge of town, and your next step is on French land.
scenes.headline: NEXT STEP IS FRANCE

scenes.narration: The reason is a treaty from 1659, the Treaty of the Pyrenees, when Spain handed France a set of villages.
scenes.headline: A TREATY FROM 1659

scenes.narration: But Llívia was counted as a town, not a village, so it was not on the list that went to France.
scenes.headline: TOWN, NOT VILLAGE

scenes.narration: One word in a treaty left a Spanish town stuck inside French land, and it has been there ever since.
scenes.headline: ONE WORD DID THIS

scenes.narration: Today it is joined to Spain by a road that is treated as neutral, and cars pass along it freely.
scenes.headline: THE NEUTRAL ROAD

scenes.narration: So you can drive from Spain to Llívia with French land on both sides of the road.
scenes.headline: FRANCE ON BOTH SIDES

scenes.narration: Think about a local. Your home is in Spain, but your neighbours across the field live in France.
scenes.headline: NEIGHBOURS, OTHER COUNTRY

scenes.narration: No giant wall divides them. Most of the time you would not even notice you had crossed the line.
scenes.headline: NO WALL AT ALL

scenes.narration: That is why border lines are about paperwork, not nature. A treaty can break a map in two.
scenes.headline: PAPERWORK, NOT NATURE

scenes.narration: If you like strange places and facts like these, subscribe, because there are plenty more coming.
scenes.headline: MORE STRANGE PLACES

scenes.narration: Number three is a tiny village that is German in law, Swiss in money, and surrounded by Switzerland.
scenes.headline: GERMANY INSIDE SWISS LAND

scenes.narration: Number three. Büsingen, a German village that sits inside Switzerland, with Swiss land on every side.
scenes.headline: BÜSINGEN

scenes.narration: It is part of Germany, but it sits right next to the Swiss city of Schaffhausen.
scenes.headline: NEAR SCHAFFHAUSEN

scenes.narration: People here pay in euros and Swiss francs, and shops often take both.
scenes.headline: TWO CURRENCIES

scenes.narration: The village is also inside Switzerland's customs area, so Swiss rules apply to many everyday goods.
scenes.headline: SWISS CUSTOMS AREA

scenes.narration: Yet the people there vote in German elections, and German law applies in many matters.
scenes.headline: GERMAN LAW AND VOTES

scenes.narration: Even the phones are mixed. The village uses the Swiss phone area code, not a German one.
scenes.headline: SWISS PHONE CODE

scenes.narration: And its car number plates start with BÜS, a code that belongs to this one small village.
scenes.headline: ITS OWN PLATE: BÜS

scenes.narration: Imagine a village where your law is German, your phone is Swiss, and your wallet holds two currencies.
scenes.headline: ONE VILLAGE, THREE SYSTEMS

scenes.narration: It exists because of old deals made centuries ago, and later talks never changed it.
scenes.headline: OLD DEALS STAYED

scenes.narration: Most of us struggle with one currency. These people handle two, plus the rules of two countries.
scenes.headline: TWO OF EVERYTHING

scenes.narration: Number two is a piece of Oman with a piece of the UAE inside it, which is inside the UAE.
scenes.headline: AN ENCLAVE IN AN ENCLAVE

scenes.narration: Number two. Madha, a piece of Oman that sits inside the United Arab Emirates, with Emirati land all around it.
scenes.headline: MADHA

scenes.narration: It lies in the mountains in the east of the UAE, away from the big glass cities.
scenes.headline: IN THE MOUNTAINS

scenes.narration: So an Omani village is surrounded by the UAE. That alone already sounds odd enough.
scenes.headline: OMAN IN THE UAE

scenes.narration: But inside Madha, there is a smaller piece of land that belongs to the UAE. It is called Nahwa.
scenes.headline: NAHWA INSIDE MADHA

scenes.narration: Nahwa is an Emirati enclave inside an Omani enclave, inside the UAE. A border inside a border inside a border.
scenes.headline: BORDER IN A BORDER

scenes.narration: On the map, it looks like a nesting doll: the UAE, then Oman, then the UAE again.
scenes.headline: A NESTING DOLL MAP

scenes.narration: Nahwa belongs to the emirate of Sharjah, even though Madha completely surrounds it.
scenes.headline: NAHWA BELONGS TO SHARJAH

scenes.narration: Reports say people there move between the pieces without much fuss, because the two countries are friendly.
scenes.headline: FRIENDLY NEIGHBOURS

scenes.narration: Lots of Indians live and work in the UAE and Oman, so this map may be closer to home than you think.
scenes.headline: CLOSE TO HOME

scenes.narration: Local tribal loyalties from long ago helped shape this map, not straight lines drawn with a ruler.
scenes.headline: SHAPED BY OLD LOYALTIES

scenes.narration: Two enclaves, one inside the other, and still not the strangest border on this list.
scenes.headline: STILL NOT THE STRANGEST

scenes.narration: Number one is in India, in the hills of Nagaland. And it runs through someone's bedroom.
scenes.headline: NEXT: A BEDROOM BORDER

scenes.narration: Number one. Longwa, a Konyak Naga village in the Mon district of Nagaland, right on the border with Myanmar.
scenes.headline: LONGWA, NAGALAND

scenes.narration: The Konyak people have lived in these hills for generations, long before this line was drawn on a map.
scenes.headline: HERE BEFORE THE LINE

scenes.narration: The border cuts through the village itself, and some homes sit on both sides of the line.
scenes.headline: A BORDER THROUGH THE VILLAGE

scenes.narration: The most famous one is the house of the Angh, which is the word for the village chief.
scenes.headline: THE ANGH'S HOUSE

scenes.narration: The India-Myanmar border runs right through the Angh's house. One part is in India, and one part is in Myanmar.
scenes.headline: HALF INDIA, HALF MYANMAR

scenes.narration: Locals like to say that in this house, you can eat in one country and sleep in another.
scenes.headline: EAT HERE, SLEEP THERE

scenes.narration: The villagers hold citizenship of both sides. A person can belong to two countries at once.
scenes.headline: CITIZENS OF BOTH

scenes.narration: For years, people here could cross without a visa under the Free Movement Regime, though India has moved to end it and fence the border.
scenes.headline: THINGS ARE CHANGING

scenes.narration: Konyak elders are known for the tattoos on their faces, and for a headhunting past that ended decades ago.
scenes.headline: FACE TATTOOS, OLD TRADITIONS

scenes.narration: A simple boundary pillar on the ground shows where India ends and Myanmar begins.
scenes.headline: THE BOUNDARY PILLAR

scenes.narration: Step across it and, for the villagers, that is just a walk to the neighbour's. For everyone else, it is another country.
scenes.headline: JUST A WALK NEXT DOOR

scenes.narration: That is why it is number one. Not the size, not the money, but a border that cuts through a family's home.
scenes.headline: WHY IT'S NUMBER ONE

scenes.narration: Quick look back: a runway, a Russian region, a Spanish town, a German village, and an enclave inside an enclave.
scenes.headline: THE FULL COUNTDOWN

scenes.narration: And at the top, a bed in Nagaland that can sit in two countries, because a line on a map ran through a family's house.
scenes.headline: A BED IN TWO COUNTRIES

scenes.narration: So remember: your night in Longwa can put your head in India and your feet in Myanmar.
scenes.headline: HEAD IN INDIA, FEET IN MYANMAR

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: more places on the map that look fake, but are completely real.
scenes.headline: TOMORROW: MORE REAL PLACES
